from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # 3D Axes setup

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        u = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=np.array([1, 2, 1]), color=BLUE)
        v = Arrow3D(start=ORIGIN, end=np.array([2, -1, 0.5]), color=RED)
        
        self.set_camera_orientation(phi=75 * DEGREES, theta=45 * DEGREES)
        self.add(axes, u, v)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        parallelogram = Polygon(
            ORIGIN, np.array([1, 2, 1]), 
            np.array([1+2, 2-1, 1+0.5]), 
            np.array([2, -1, 0.5]), 
            color=PURPLE, fill_opacity=0.3
        )
        self.add(parallelogram)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Geometric Intuition & Determinants", [
            "The cross product is a determinant.",
            "Zero area means vectors are collinear.",
            "It measures how independent vectors are."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        vec_a = Vector([1.5, 0.5], color=BLUE)
        vec_b = Vector([0.5, 1.5], color=RED)
        parallelogram = Polygon([0, 0, 0], [1.5, 0.5, 0], [2.0, 2.0, 0], [0.5, 1.5, 0], 
                               fill_color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=2)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"|\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}| = \det\begin{pmatrix} a_x & b_x \\ a_y & b_y \end{pmatrix}", font_size=32)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(parallelogram, 'C2')
        self.play(Create(parallelogram))
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E4')
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Flatten vectors to simulate collinearity
        vec_a_new = Vector([1.5, 0.5], color=BLUE)
        vec_b_new = Vector([0.75, 0.25], color=RED)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(parallelogram, Polygon([0, 0, 0], [1.5, 0.5, 0], [0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0], 
                                            fill_color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.1)),
            run_time=2
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Linear Transformations and Orientation", ["Cross products define linear transformations.", "They map vectors to a new space.", "This preserves coordinate system handedness."])
        
        # Define objects
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3})
        vec_i = Vector(RIGHT, color=BLUE)
        vec_j = Vector(UP, color=RED)
        
        # Initial state
        transform_group = VGroup(grid, vec_i, vec_j)
        self.place_in_area(transform_group, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(transform_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform basis
        matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        self.play(ApplyMatrix(matrix, transform_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show Handedness
        label = Text("Preserved Handedness", font_size=20, color=GREEN)

        self.play(Write(label))

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Application", [
            "Cross product equals perpendicular vector area.",
            "It is crucial for calculating torque.",
            "Force times lever arm yields rotation."
        ])
        
        # Animation Elements
        wrench = VGroup(
            Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 2, stroke_width=8, color=GRAY),
            Circle(radius=0.3, color=GRAY).shift(RIGHT * 2)
        )
        bolt = Dot(color=YELLOW).shift(RIGHT * 2)
        force_vec = Arrow(start=RIGHT*2 + UP*0.5, end=RIGHT*2 + UP*1.8, color=BLUE, buff=0)
        torque_vec = Arrow(start=RIGHT*2, end=RIGHT*2 + OUT*1.5, color=RED, buff=0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        area = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=PURPLE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(area, 'B3')
        self.play(FadeIn(area))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(wrench, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(bolt, 'D3')
        self.play(FadeIn(wrench), FadeIn(bolt))
        self.play(GrowArrow(force_vec))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        self.play(GrowArrow(torque_vec))
        self.play(Rotate(wrench, angle=PI/6, about_point=self.grid['D3']))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Geometric Intuition of the Cross Product

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors in 3D Space
sections.content: Briefly define vectors as directed segments in 3D space. Introduce the concept of a 'parallelogram' spanned by two vectors, u and v, as the geometric foundation for the cross product.
sections.example: Imagine two robotic arms positioned at the origin, pointing in different directions; the space between them represents the 'tent' or parallelogram we aim to measure.

sections.title: Definition of the Cross Product
sections.content: Introduce the cross product result as a vector perpendicular to the original plane. Use the Right-Hand Rule to determine the direction. Emphasize that the magnitude equals the area of the parallelogram formed by the two input vectors.
sections.example: A spinning propeller blade: the vectors follow the blade, while the cross-product vector points straight out along the axle, indicating the axis of rotation.

sections.title: Geometric Intuition & Determinants
sections.content: Visualize the cross product as a determinant calculation. Explain that if the area (determinant) is zero, the vectors are collinear (overlapping). This provides a intuitive measure of 'how parallel' or 'how independent' vectors are.
sections.example: A digital artist using a 3D modeling tool: dragging two vectors—if they are perfectly aligned, the cross product vanishes, signaling the 'collapse' of the 3D surface area.

sections.title: Linear Transformations and Orientation
sections.content: Explain the cross product as a linear transformation where the input vectors are mapped to a new space. Discuss how the cross product preserves (or flips) the orientation (handedness) of the coordinate system.
sections.example: A character in a video game moving through a portal: the cross product helps calculate the surface normal, ensuring the character walks on the ground rather than falling through the wall.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Recap: Cross product = Perpendicular vector + Area calculation. Connect this to real-world physics, such as torque (force x lever arm) which is the classic application of this geometric relationship.
sections.example: An animation of a wrench tightening a bolt: the 'force' vector and 'lever arm' vector combine via cross product to show the resulting torque vector moving the bolt forward.
